userStories.title: Expose the catalog, expanded role keys and binding filters
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Supply catalog metadata, safe expanded role keys and principal-type/global binding reads.

**Motivation** — The catalog (risk, scope, ownability) is code-only; and `GET /role-bindings` cannot list "every agent's global bindings" in one filter.

**Approach** — - New controller `PermissionCatalogController` in `apps/api/src/permissions/permission-catalog.controller.ts`, registered in `PermissionsModule.controllers`: `GET /permissions/catalog`, `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('role.read')`. It returns `PermissionCatalogEntryDto[]` for every `PERMISSION_CATALOG` entry whose `access` is `'role'`, sorted by `key`:

```ts
class PermissionCatalogEntryDto { key: string; scope: 'global' | 'project' | 'any'; risk: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'critical'; principals: ('user' | 'agent')[]; ownable: boolean }
```

- `RoleDto` gains `expandedKeys: string[]`: `expandEntries(role.permissions, role.scope)` as a sorted array, or `[]` when the stored entries no longer expand (`expandEntries` throws). Every route that returns a `RoleDto` carries it.
- `ListRoleBindingsQuery` changes:
  - `principalType` alone is now accepted and filters by type; `principalId` alone is still refused (400 validation).
  - New `scope?: 'global'`: only `projectId`-null bindings. Any other value is a 400 validation error, and `scope=global` together with a non-empty `projectId` is a 400 validation error with key `permissions.scopeAndProject`.
  - `BindingFilter` gains `principalType?: PrincipalType`; `MembershipService.listBindings`, `PrismaRoleBindingRepository` and the test double `InMemoryPermissionStore` (`apps/api/src/permissions/test-helpers/in-memory-permissions.ts`) honour it. `projectId: null` in the filter already means "global bindings only".

New API error keys get messages in both `en` and `zh`, under both the `-2` and `400` status keys as `permissions.scopeMismatch` has them: `permissions.scopeAndProject` (`permissions.json`). Exceptions are `new XAppException({}, '<namespace>.<code>')`, with messages at `<namespace>.<code>.<status>`.

**Scope** — In: catalog DTO/controller/module, common RoleDto serialization, query/controller/filter/repository/test-double propagation, localized scope conflict, endpoint inventory and existing binding/unit regressions. Out: project role listing and members (US-003), browser editor (US-010), binding browser (US-011), OpenAPI export (US-005).

**Interface** — `RoleDto` target `{ id, key, name, description, scope, system, locked, permissions, expandedKeys: string[] }`; `ListRoleBindingsQuery` target accepts `principalType` alone and `scope?: 'global'`; `BindingFilter` gains `principalType?: PrincipalType`.

userStories.title: List assignable project roles and unified user/agent members
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let member.read holders load project roles and paginated users/agents with local binding chips.

**Motivation** — `role.read` is a global key, so a Project Admin cannot list roles or bindings.

**Approach** — - `RoleAdminService.listProjectRoles(): Promise<RoleDomain[]>` (new, public): every role with `scope = 'PROJECT'`, system roles first, then by `key`. It checks no key: its route's guard does.
- New controller `ProjectRolesController` in `apps/api/src/projects/members/project-roles.controller.ts`, registered in `ProjectMembersModule`: `GET /projects/:slug/roles`, `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('member.read')`. It returns `ProjectRoleDto { id, key, name, description, system }[]` from `listProjectRoles()`.
- `GET /projects/:slug/members` takes `principals?: 'users' | 'all'` (default `users`; any other value is 400 validation).
  - `ProjectMemberDto` changes: `userId: string | null` (null for agents), `email: string | null` (null for agents), plus `principalType: 'USER' | 'AGENT'`, `principalId: string`, `agentSlug: string | null` (null for users), `bindings: MemberBindingDto[]`. `name`, `role`, `disabled` and `joinedAt` keep their meaning; for an agent `name` is `Agent.name`, `disabled` is `false`, and `role` is the strongest legacy role of its sources as `listProjectMemberships` reports it.
  - `MemberBindingDto { id: string | null; roleKey: string; roleName: string }`: one entry per `RoleBinding` of that principal **in this project** (`projectId` equal), ordered by `createdAt`. Then the legacy rows, read directly for the page's principals: a `ProjectMember` row (`projectMember.findMany` by `projectId` and the page's user ids) maps its `role` through `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE` (`ADMIN` → `project-admin`, `DEVELOPER` → `developer`, `VIEWER` → `viewer`; any other value → `viewer`), and an `AgentProject` row (`agentProject.findMany`, which has no role column) maps to `viewer`. A legacy row adds one entry with `id: null` only when the principal has no binding of that key in the project. All-projects bindings are not listed here.
  - The single-record responses carry the same shape with `bindings` populated: `POST /projects/:slug/members`, the legacy `PATCH /projects/:slug/members/:userId`, and the `member` of an invite's `ADDED` outcome. `ProjectMemberRecord` (the shared domain type in `domain/project-member.domain.ts`) gains `principalType`, `principalId`, `agentSlug` and `bindings`, and `userId` / `email` become `string | null`; `ProjectMemberDto.from(record)` copies them.
  - With `principals=all`, the page is the user rows (in today's order) followed by the agent rows (`listProjectMemberships(db, projectId, 'AGENT')`, same order rule); `total` counts both.
  - `canManage` and `viewerRole` stay in the response unchanged (drop-legacy removes them).

**Scope** — In: service/controller/module/repository/domain/DTO enrichment, combined pagination before slicing, all single-record producers, member service/controller/DI unit fixtures and route inventory case. Out: grant helper/roleKey member writes (US-004), invite role migration (US-005), browser management panel (US-013). All-projects bindings are not shown or edited in a project's member list; they are managed on Admin → Users and Admin → Agents.

**Interface** — `RoleAdminService.listProjectRoles(): Promise<RoleDomain[]>`; `ProjectMembersService.list(slug, principal, page, principals: 'users' | 'all')` with omitted principals defaulting to 'users'; `MemberBindingDto { id: string | null; roleKey: string; roleName: string }`; `ProjectRoleDto { id, key, name, description, system }`.

userStories.title: Grant member role keys through shared escalation rules
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Secure custom-role and legacy member grants and support role-less admin user creation.

**Motivation** — A Triager, an Approver or any custom role is a first-class binding.

**Approach** — US-004 owns `assertMayGrant`, the member add and `CreateUserDto`; US-005 owns everything about invites and the `openapi.json` regeneration.

- `RoleAdminService.assertMayGrant(principal, target: { roleKey: string; projectId: string | null; principalType: PrincipalType; principalId: string | null }): Promise<RoleDomain>` (new, public). It runs the binding rules that do not need an existing target row, in this order, and returns the role:
  1. role lookup by key: 404 `permissions.roleNotFound`;
  2. a GLOBAL role with a project id: 400 `permissions.scopeMismatch`;
  3. principal type: 400 `permissions.principalType` (as `assertPrincipalType`);
  4. self: when `principalId` equals the caller's id and type, 403 `permissions.selfBinding`;
  5. escalation: 403 `permissions.escalation` (as `createBinding`'s `assertNoEscalation`, scope from `projectId`).

  It does not check `role.binding.manage` / `role.binding.global`: the calling route's own key (`member.add`, `invite.create`) is the gate. `createBinding` keeps its own checks unchanged.
- `POST /projects/:slug/members`: `AddMemberDto` gains `roleKey?: string` (`ROLE_KEY_PATTERN`); both fields are optional in the DTO. The service throws `ValidationAppException({}, 'members.roleAndRoleKey')` when both are sent; neither means `viewer`, as today. The effective key is `roleKey`, else `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE[role]`, else `viewer`. After the user lookup (404 `members.user`, 409 `members.userDisabled`), `ProjectMembersService.add` calls `assertMayGrant(principal, { roleKey: <effective key>, projectId, principalType: 'USER', principalId: user.id })` on every path, then writes the binding with that key inside the existing transaction (409 `members` when already a member).
- `CreateUserDto.role` becomes optional (default `'MEMBER'`), so the web creates a user and then binds roles. `UsersAdminService.create` and its input type treat an absent `role` as `'MEMBER'`.
- New API error keys get messages in both `en` and `zh`, under both the `-2` and `400` status keys as `permissions.scopeMismatch` has them: `members.roleAndRoleKey` (`members.json`).

Both write routes use one order: user lookup, then 409 for a disabled existing account (`invites.userDisabled` / `members.userDisabled`), then `assertMayGrant`, then 409 for an existing member (`invites.memberExists` / `members`). Order of checks on every write route: (1) the permission key, (2) input validation and lookups, (3) self-binding, (4) escalation, (5) Owner lock. `ProjectMembersService` constructor adds `RoleAdminService` as the last parameter; update service and DI doubles and optional-role DTO tests.

**Scope** — In: shared helper and unchanged createBinding checks, member custom/legacy/default role grant, optional CreateUserDto/service/input role default, messages and unit/integration changes. Out: applying the helper to invites and schema migration (US-005), browser forms (US-011/013). Legacy role fields/routes remain for the CLI.

**Interface** — `RoleAdminService.assertMayGrant(principal, target: { roleKey: string; projectId: string | null; principalType: PrincipalType; principalId: string | null }): Promise<RoleDomain>`; `AddMemberDto.roleKey?: string`; `CreateUserDto.role` optional, default `'MEMBER'`.

userStories.title: Persist and accept invite role keys and export the API contract
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry project role identities through invite creation, preview, mail and acceptance without breaking legacy invites.

**Motivation** — The members panel and the invites panel offer only ADMIN/DEVELOPER/VIEWER.

**Approach** — US-004 owns `assertMayGrant`, the member add and `CreateUserDto`; US-005 owns everything about invites and the `openapi.json` regeneration.

- `POST /projects/:slug/invites`: `CreateInviteDto.role` becomes optional and gains `roleKey?: string`; both are optional in the DTO, and the service requires exactly one (both: `ValidationAppException({}, 'invites.roleAndRoleKey')`; neither: `ValidationAppException({}, 'invites.roleRequired')`). The effective key is `roleKey`, else `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE[role]`. Both write routes use one order: user lookup, then 409 for a disabled existing account (`invites.userDisabled` / `members.userDisabled`), then `assertMayGrant`, then 409 for an existing member (`invites.memberExists` / `members`). `ProjectInvitesService.create` calls `assertMayGrant(principal, { roleKey: <effective key>, projectId, principalType: 'USER', principalId: existingUserId ?? null })` at that point on both paths; `addExistingUser` binds that role key and `inviteNewAddress` stores the invite with `roleId`.
- Schema: `ProjectInvite.roleId String?` with `assignedRole Role? @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)` (and `invites ProjectInvite[]` on `Role`); `ProjectInvite.role String?` (nullable). Migration `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261101090000_invite_role_id/migration.sql`. A new invite stores `roleId` and stores `role` only when its key is `project-admin`, `developer` or `viewer` (the legacy enum the key maps to), else null. The spec's illustrative relation was also named `role`; that cannot coexist with the retained `role` scalar in Prisma. Use the internal relation name `assignedRole` and update repository includes/mapping accordingly, keeping the scalar, FK semantics and HTTP fields unchanged.
- Invite acceptance (`InviteAcceptanceService`) binds the role named by `roleId`; a row with `roleId` null binds `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE[role]`; a row with both null answers 409 `invites.roleGone`.
- `InviteDto` and `InvitePreviewDto` gain `roleKey: string | null` and `roleName: string | null` (from `roleId`'s role, else from the legacy `role` mapping, else null); `role` becomes `string | null`. The invite email passes `roleName` as the existing `{{role}}` placeholder value; the templates are unchanged.
- New API error keys get messages in both `en` and `zh`, under both the `-2` and `400` status keys as `permissions.scopeMismatch` has them: `invites.roleAndRoleKey`, `invites.roleRequired`, `invites.roleGone` (`invites.json`).
- `openapi.json` is regenerated with `bun run api:export-spec` in US-005, after the last API contract change.

`assertMayGrant` also runs when a caller sends only the legacy `role` (mapped to its key through `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE`), so the CLI path gets the same escalation and self-binding rules as `roleKey`. `ProjectInvitesService` constructor adds `RoleAdminService` as the last parameter. Update GlobalStubsModule, repository/domain/create inputs, DTOs, acceptance/member result fixtures and invite mailer inputs; preserve transaction/claim/cache/session and token-secrecy behavior. The invite list gains roleKey/roleName (nine keys), preview gains them (eight keys), with no token/tokenHash leakage. Exceptions are `new XAppException({}, '<namespace>.<code>')` with localized status messages.

**Scope** — In: invites' helper use, migration, nullable role fields, legacy fallback, roleName mail value and OpenAPI export after all API changes. Out: helper definition and member writes (US-004), web invite panels (US-014). The MEMBER_ADDED email (`email-content.builder.ts`) still shows the legacy role string; giving it the role name is out of scope. The CLI (`apps/cli`) and its generated client are not changed; the CLI keeps the legacy `role` flags until a CLI follow-up. `apps/cli/src/generated/` is not regenerated. US-005 only: an existing pending invite created before the migration keeps `roleId` null and is accepted through its legacy `role`; no backfill.

**Interface** — `CreateInviteDto { role?: ProjectMemberRole; roleKey?: string }`; `InviteDto` / `InvitePreviewDto` target `role: string | null; roleKey: string | null; roleName: string | null`; `ProjectInvite.roleId String?`; `assignedRole Role? @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)`; the legacy scalar remains `role String?`.

userStories.title: Add SSR permission sets and key-based global navigation gates
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add fail-closed SSR permission composables and replace the global role-name navigation gates.

**Motivation** — The admin navigation, the command palette and the knowledge card check `auth.user.role === 'ADMIN'`.

**Approach** — `apps/web/lib/permissions.ts` (new):

```ts
export interface PermissionSet {
  /** Holds the key for every row. */
  has(key: string): boolean
```

userStories.title: Build Admin Roles CRUD with the permission matrix editor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let authorized humans browse and manage data-driven roles through a catalog-backed editor.

**Motivation** — There is no page for roles at all, so custom roles exist only through the REST API.

**Approach** — - `pages/admin/roles.vue` (new), `composables/useRoles.ts` (new: `load()`, `create(input)`, `update(id, patch)`, `remove(id)`, `loadCatalog()` over `/roles` and `/permissions/catalog`), `components/RoleEditorDialog.vue` (new), `components/PermissionMatrix.vue` (new).
- The list shows name, key, scope, a `system` badge and a `locked` badge. A 403 on `GET /roles` shows the page's admin-only message, like `pages/admin/users.vue`.
- The editor: key (create only, `ROLE_KEY_PATTERN`), name, description, scope (create only) and permissions.
  - Matrix rows: catalog entries whose `scope` fits the role (`GLOBAL` → `global` or `any`; `PROJECT` → `project` or `any`), grouped by the key's first segment, each with its `risk` as a badge.
  - A non-ownable row is a checkbox; an ownable row is a three-way choice none / own / any, writing `X.own` or `X`.
  - Entries that are not a plain key of a matrix row (wildcards like `*.read`, `prefix.*`, exclusions `!x`) are kept verbatim as removable chips, and a text input adds one.
  - For a saved role, a row whose key is in `expandedKeys` but not an explicit entry shows checked and disabled ("covered").
  - Save sends `permissions` as the chip entries in their stored order, then the checked keys sorted.
- A `locked` role opens read-only (no save, no delete). A `system` role's name is read-only and it has no delete; a save omits `name`.
- Create, edit and delete controls show only with `role.manage` (global); the nav link `/admin/roles` shows with `role.read` (global).

Every new composable (`useGlobalPermissions`, `useProjectPermissions`, `useRoles`, `useRoleBindings`, `useProjectRoles`) is added to the `NUXT_AUTO_IMPORTS` override list in `tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts` by the story that creates it. New components (`RoleEditorDialog`, `PermissionMatrix`, `PrincipalRolesDialog`) are imported explicitly in the SFCs that use them, as `pages/agents.vue` imports its dialogs. Every web story that renders a new string adds its key to both `i18n/locales/en.json` and `zh.json`. A web gate only hides or disables a control; every refusal from the API is still shown with `toast.error(extractApiError(err))`. When a role write fails, the list keeps its last loaded state and the dialog stays open. Reuse ApiError ret 40003 detection, useApi/apiPath, vee-validate/zod and existing dialog patterns; preserve inline nav/source order, plain per-link booleans and fail-closed section label. Keep .own choices explicitly editable while treating wildcard/exclusion entries as ordered chips.

**Scope** — In: roles page/composable/editor/matrix, role-read nav, system/locked safeguards, catalog reads, sorted explicit-key writes, locales and helper override. Out: role bindings dialogs/principal pages (US-011/012). A preview of an unsaved wildcard's effect in the role editor is out of scope; covered rows reflect the saved role's `expandedKeys`. P2 audit and P3 policy pages remain deferred.

**Interface** — `useRoles`: `load()`, `create(input)`, `update(id, patch)`, `remove(id)`, `loadCatalog()` over `/roles` and `/permissions/catalog`; role records carry `{ id, key, name, description, scope, system, locked, permissions, expandedKeys: string[] }`; catalog records carry `{ key, scope, risk, principals, ownable }`.

  - Add an agent: select from `GET /agents` minus agents already listed, plus a role → `POST /role-bindings { principalType: 'AGENT', principalId, roleKey, projectId }`.
